advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `_criterion_id` case for a dash-containing project name (e.g. assert `_criterion_id("plan-review-project-foo-bar", root) == "project.foo-bar"`) so only the namespace-boundary dash is restored.
evidence: Overlay permits interior dashes: `if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*", name)` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:145)
Fix restores only the first dash: `dotted = "project." + cid[len("project-") :]` (src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:85)

All test fixtures use the dash-free name `testcrit`: `_EVAL = {"prompt": "plan-review-project-testcrit", ...}` and `overlay = {"plan_review": {"project.testcrit": _ROUTING}, ...}` (tests/unit/test_eval_solver_project_criterion.py:47, :75) — no case with an interior dash exists
ABSENCE: no assertion of the form `_criterion_id("plan-review-project-foo-bar", root) == "project.foo-bar"`, so a full-dash-replace mutation of the fix would survive the suite
advisory.finding: The new tests never exercise a project criterion whose name CONTAINS a dash (e.g. `project.foo-bar` → `plan-review-project-foo-bar`), which is the distinguishing edge case the fix's single-dash restoration handles. A naive implementation replacing ALL dashes (`cid.replace('-', '.')`) would still pass every current assertion, so the interior-dash regression is untested.
scenarios: A user defines a project criterion `project.my-check`; the eval path resolves its physical id `plan-review-project-my-check` back to the correct dotted logical id
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fixture/overlay with a dashed name (e.g. `project.foo-bar`) and assert `eval_solver._criterion_id("plan-review-project-foo-bar", root) == "project.foo-bar"`, pinning that interior dashes are preserved.
